title: Online Meetings
goal: Check participation in an online meeting, take a turn and explain a connection or screen-sharing problem.

runs.text: Mute
stops your microphone sending sound in the meeting;
unmute
allows it again.
Share your screen
lets others see selected screen content through the meeting system.
Chat
refers to the meeting's text-message area. Use the platform's actual controls when needed; these models practice the conversation around them.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: Hi, everyone. Can you hear me?

turns.en: Hi, everyone. Can you hear me?

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Yes, I can. Can you hear me?

turns.en: Yes, I can. Can you hear me?

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: Yes. Let's get started. I'll share the agenda.

turns.en: Yes. Let's get started. I'll share the agenda.

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: I can see the agenda, but the text is small.

turns.en: I can see the agenda, but the text is small.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: I'll enlarge it. Is that better?

turns.en: I'll enlarge it. Is that better?

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Yes, thanks.

turns.en: Yes, thanks.

runs.text: Supported responses include
I can hear you
I can't hear you
I can see the screen
, and
I can only see your name
. Explain which part is working rather than saying only
It's broken

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: Who would like to comment first?

turns.en: Who would like to comment first?

turns.speaker: Maya

runs.text: Could I go first? I have a question about the schedule.

turns.en: Could I go first? I have a question about the schedule.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: Go ahead.

turns.en: Go ahead.

turns.speaker: Maya

runs.text: Does the trial start this week or next week?

turns.en: Does the trial start this week or next week?

turns.speaker: Lee

runs.text: Sorry, I interrupted. Please continue.

turns.en: Sorry, I interrupted. Please continue.

turns.speaker: Maya

runs.text: Thanks. I was asking which week it starts.

turns.en: Thanks. I was asking which week it starts.

blocks.caption: Take a turn · Host & Maya & Lee

runs.text: Go ahead
gives the other person the turn.
Please continue
returns it after an interruption. When talking overlaps:
I think we spoke at the same time. You go first
helps reset the exchange. You can also say
Could I finish my question?
if you need to keep the turn.

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Your audio is cutting out. I missed the last part.

turns.en: Your audio is cutting out. I missed the last part.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: Which part did you hear?

turns.en: Which part did you hear?

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: I heard “the trial starts,” but not the date. Could you repeat it?

turns.en: I heard “the trial starts,” but not the date. Could you repeat it?

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: It starts Monday. I'll put that in the chat as well.

turns.en: It starts Monday. I'll put that in the chat as well.

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Thanks. Monday, got it.

turns.en: Thanks. Monday, got it.

runs.text: Cutting out
or
breaking up
describes interrupted sound.
The screen is frozen
describes an image that has stopped updating.
I got disconnected
explains leaving unintentionally. A text route can help:
Could you put the key point in the chat?

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Sorry, I got disconnected. What did I miss?

turns.en: Sorry, I got disconnected. What did I miss?

turns.speaker: Coworker

runs.text: We confirmed the Monday start.

turns.en: We confirmed the Monday start.

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Thanks. Was anything assigned to me?

turns.en: Thanks. Was anything assigned to me?

turns.speaker: Coworker

runs.text: Not yet. We're discussing that now.

turns.en: Not yet. We're discussing that now.

runs.text: These are written role-play lines. Reading them does not test whether you can hear an actual poor connection; real listening practice comes with audio.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: We'll meet again next Tuesday at three.

turns.en: We'll meet again next Tuesday at three.

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Could you include the time zone in the invitation?

turns.en: Could you include the time zone in the invitation?

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: Yes, I'll include it.

turns.en: Yes, I'll include it.

turns.speaker: Participant

runs.text: Thanks. Could you also send the action-item summary?

turns.en: Thanks. Could you also send the action-item summary?

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: I will.

turns.en: I will.

blocks.caption: Confirm the next step · Host & Participant

runs.text: Which time zone is that?
asks an important missing detail.
Would you send an invite?
requests the meeting information instead of assuming everyone already has it.
Read the host or coworker's line and respond aloud. Alone, switch roles. No live meeting or recording is needed.
The host asks whether you can hear and see the agenda. You can hear, but cannot see the screen. State both facts.
You missed the date after
The trial starts...
Request that specific part and ask for it in the chat.
You return after disconnecting. Ask what you missed and whether a task was assigned to you.
A participant interrupts your question. Ask to finish, or give them the turn and return to your question afterward.
The next meeting is Tuesday at 3, but no time zone was stated. Ask for it and an invitation.
Sample possibilities:

“I can hear you, but I can't see the agenda.” / “Could you repeat the start date and put it in the chat?” / “What did I miss? Was anything assigned to me?” / “Could I finish my question?” / “Which time zone is that? Could you send an invite?”
Repeat later with a different missing detail. Check whether your explanation identified the problem and enabled the other person to repair the communication.
